title: Congruence Classes of Supporting the Erdös-Straus Conjecture II: Wild Solutions
summary: In 1948, Erdös and Straus formulated a conjecture : for any positive integer $n>2$, there exist positive integers $n_1,n_2$ and $n_3$ such that \begin{equation}\frac{4}{n}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\frac{1}{n_2}+\frac{1}{n_3},\nonumber\end{equation} which is still open. It is known that the conjecture holds if one can prove it for any prime $n\equiv 1\;(\mbox{mod}\;24)$. If $n=24m+1$ and $n_1\leq n_2,n_3$, then $n_1=6m+k$ with $1\leq k\leq 12m$. A solution $(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ of the above equation is called a {\it tame solution} if $n_2$ and $n_3$ are factors of $(6m+k)(24m+1)$. We call $n=24m+1$ {\it wild}…
